segments.line: Nine pm.. The police station.
No loading screen. No skip button.
They take your fingerprints, one finger at a time.
Your photo, front and side.
Everything in your pockets goes into a plastic bag. Including a napkin from hot dog number six.
In the game, this takes three seconds. In real life, getting booked can take hours.
Then they put you in a holding cell. A metal bench. A toilet with no seat. A
man in the corner who keeps asking what time it is.
Every few minutes, you check for the stars. There are no stars.
There's just a clock on the wall, and it is very slow.
Then, the phone call. You've heard everybody gets one phone call.
Actually, that's not a real rule everywhere. It depends on where you are.
But tonight, they let you call.
You stare at the phone. You could call Mo. Mo would think this is hilarious.
Or you could call your mom.
Mom picks up on the first ring. Because she saw the video. Everyone saw the video.
So now there's one choice left. Say it was a joke. Just a game. No big deal. Or tell her the truth. Every single thing.
You take a breath. And you tell her everything. The fence. The taxi. The car. The six hot dogs.
You hear her car keys. You hear her shoes. Then you hear her say your full name. All three parts of it.
There's a long silence. Then, very quietly: I'm coming. Somehow, that's scarier than the dog.
